audit.whatIsWrong: Both layers call Quinn's Vault (E) a 'knock-back'. Riot's own text says Quinn 'leaps off the target, briefly interrupting it, and lands near her maximum Attack Range away' — Zac is not displaced at all.
audit.why: The distinction changes how you play it. A knockback would mean Zac gets pushed out of range; what actually happens is Quinn's leap interrupts Zac's Elastic Slingshot charge and she ends up ~575 units further out. The counterplay is to charge E from a position she cannot Vault into, not to brace for displacement.
audit.corrected: Vault (E) does not displace Zac. It dashes to him, applies a slow and a brief interrupt that cancels his E charge, and lands Quinn near her max attack range away. Cooldown 12/11/10/9/8s.
sources: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json (Riot Data Dragon, Vault description + cooldown)

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing in either layer mentions Heightened Senses (W). Its active reveals a large area at 2100 range — it is the single hardest counter to Zac's signature fog/bush Elastic Slingshot, and both layers tell the Zac player to 'E from fog' with no caveat.
audit.why: Zac's entire engage pattern in this lane is charging E unseen. A Quinn who holds W denies that outright, and the ability sits on a 50s cooldown at rank 1 — the longest basic-ability cooldown in her kit and by far the biggest punish window in the matchup. Telling a Zac to E from fog without telling him W exists sends him into a revealed charge.
audit.corrected: Heightened Senses (W) actives a large-area reveal (2100 range) on a 50/45/40/35/30s cooldown. If she has burned it, your bush charge is genuinely hidden; if it is up, assume the fog engage is seen.

audit.whatIsWrong: content whys[2] claims 'Level 3 her double-Q blind plus Vault burst'. Blinding Assault is on an 11s cooldown at rank 1 — there is no double-Q at level 3.
audit.why: It invents a burst pattern that cannot happen and hides the real number. Her Q is the longest-range thing in the lane (1025 vs your 800 Q) but it comes once every 11s at rank 1, which is the actual trade window.
audit.corrected: Blinding Assault: 11/10.5/10/9.5/9s. One cast per trade at rank 1, not two.

audit.whatIsWrong: full phases[4].why for Level 6 is boilerplate ('Elastic Slingshot from fog + R bounces win every river fight') that is pasted verbatim into every Zac matchup and says nothing about Behind Enemy Lines.
audit.why: Quinn's level 6 is the one stage where the correct play is not a fight at all — her R is a roam/reposition tool, so the Zac response is tempo (shove, plates, ping) rather than an all-in. The generic line actively pushes a river fight she can simply leave.
audit.corrected: Behind Enemy Lines is a channelled travel ultimate, not a duelling one — she leaves lane with it. Punish the tempo instead of chasing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/quinn.json (Behind Enemy Lines: channel flag, Skystrike on exit)

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on the level chart. content win[] is [Quinn, Quinn, Quinn, Zac, Quinn, Skill, Zac] (Quinn 4 / Zac 2 / Skill 1); full phases[].side is [Quinn, Skill, Zac, Zac, Quinn, Zac, Zac] (Zac 4 / Quinn 2 / Skill 1). Zac's win rate here is 60.71% over 56 games.
audit.why: A 60.71% matchup should not read as Quinn owning four of seven stages. The full layer's split is the one consistent with the data, so the content chart is the side that is wrong.
audit.corrected: Align content win[1] and win[2] to the full layer, giving Quinn levels 1 and 6 (her real windows) and Zac the mid-lane and item stages.

notes: Two verified naming/mechanic errors fixed: Vault is an interrupt, not a knockback, and there is no 'double-Q' at level 3 (Blinding Assault is 11s at rank 1). The biggest genuine gap was Heightened Senses (W) — a 2100-range area reveal on a 50s rank-1 cooldown that hard-counters Zac's fog Elastic Slingshot; neither layer mentioned it anywhere. LAYER DISAGREEMENT (not fully edited): content win[] gives Quinn 4/7 stages while full phases[].side gives Zac 4/7, for a matchup Zac wins 60.71% over 56 games. I aligned win[1] and win[2] via their whys but did not touch the win[] array itself — recommend the applier reconcile the two charts wholesale, since editing side/win entries without their paired prose risks incoherence. Also note full.diff is TRICKY at 7.5/10 for a 60.71% win rate; that rating looks too harsh but I have no verifiable basis to pick a replacement number, so I left it.
